name: Battle of Marengo
note: The accounts give the places of the villages only as a triangle (Marengo west, Castel Ceriolo north, San Giuliano Vecchio east), so distances here are schematic. The accounts do not say where Kellermann's cavalry stood before its last charge; it is placed on the northern side of the Austrian column. Frimont's cavalry, which destroyed the Guard, is drawn with the Austrian left wing, with which the accounts have him act. The accounts do not say where the supporting dragoons stood; they are placed beside the Austrian column on its northern side, with Pilatti’s troopers drawn as part of the same block.

phases.title: The two armies take their ground
phases.text: The Austrians crossed the Bormida in three bodies. Victor held Marengo and the Fontanone with Kellermann's cavalry on his left, Lannes stood to the north-east, and Monnier and the Guard waited east of Castel Ceriolo.
phases.quote: The movement began about 6 am with the first shots fired around 8 am, but the attack was not fully developed until 9 am.

phases.title: The Austrian assaults at the Fontanone fail
phases.text: Melas sent his divisions at Marengo across the stream one after another. Forced into a funnel by the ground, the first attack failed under fire from two sides, and the second was beaten off by 11 am.
phases.quote: Forced into a funnel by the bad ground and Fontanone stream, Hadik's attack came under fire from two sides and failed, with Hadik being killed.

phases.title: Ott takes Castel Ceriolo and presses the French right
phases.text: Ott's leading troops took Castel Ceriolo and began to press the French right flank. Monnier's division and the Guard were brought across to extend and shore up that flank.
phases.quote: but soon Ott's lead units took it around 11:30 am and began putting pressure on the French right flank

phases.title: The Austrians bridge the Fontanone and take Stortiglione
phases.text: A small bridge was thrown over the Fontanone under cover of reserve artillery, and Lattermann's grenadiers crossed to attack the French defending Marengo village. O'Reilly took Stortiglione by 2:00 pm.
phases.quote: A Laufbrücke (small bridge) was thrown over the Fontanone and supported by reserve artillery.

phases.title: Victor withdraws to the vines
phases.text: Victor could no longer hold his positions and fell back south-east to the main belt of vines, with Lannes mirroring the move.
phases.quote: However, Victor could no longer hold his positions and withdrew southeast to the main vine belt

phases.title: Ott defeats Monnier
phases.text: Ott, aided by Frimont, defeated Monnier's division and forced two thirds of it to retreat to the north-east, away from the main French army.
phases.quote: Aided by Frimont, Ott defeated Monnier and forced two-thirds of his command to retreat to the northeast.

phases.title: The Consular Guard is destroyed
phases.text: Bonaparte sent his main Guard battalion and its artillery to flank the Austrian column and delay it. After a firefight of fifteen minutes the Guard was surprised and destroyed by Frimont's cavalry.
phases.quote: After a 15-minute firefight around 4:00 pm the Guard were surprised and destroyed by Frimont's cavalry.

phases.title: The French fall back towards San Giuliano
phases.text: The French fell back about 3 km and tried to regroup at San Giuliano. The Austrian centre formed into a pursuit column to chase them off the field.
phases.quote: The French fell back c. 3 km and attempted to regroup to hold the village of San Giuliano.

phases.title: Desaix's force arrives and meets the column
phases.text: Boudet's division was deployed in front of San Giuliano and advanced in line of brigades against the head of the Austrian column, defeating its leading brigade. The column came on along the road.
phases.quote: Boudet's division advanced in line of brigades against the head of the Austrian column, defeating Saint-Julien's leading Austrian brigade.

phases.title: Lattermann's grenadiers renew the attack
phases.text: The Austrian staff brought up Lattermann's grenadier brigade in line and renewed the attack, with a dragoon regiment in support.
phases.quote: Zach brought forward GM Lattermann's grenadier brigade in line and renewed the attack.

phases.title: Desaix is sent forward and the cavalry is ordered in
phases.text: Faced with a crisis, Napoleon sent Desaix forward again and ordered the cavalry charge that Desaix had asked for.
phases.quote: Faced with a crisis, Napoleon sent Desaix forward again and ordered a cavalry charge requested by Desaix.

phases.title: Kellermann's charge breaks the grenadiers
phases.text: Lattermann's formation was charged on its left flank by Kellermann's heavy cavalry, about 400 men, and disintegrated.
phases.quote: Lattermann's formation was charged on its left flank by Kellermann's heavy cavalry (ca. 400 men) and disintegrated.

phases.title: The supporting dragoons are routed
phases.text: Murat and Kellermann at once attacked the supporting Liechtenstein Dragoons, which were too slow to respond, and routed them. The fleeing horsemen crashed into Pilatti's troopers and carried them away.
phases.quote: Murat and Kellermann immediately pounced on the supporting Liechtenstein Dragoons who were too slow to respond and routed them as well.

phases.title: The Austrian main body breaks and the French advance
phases.text: As the terrified cavalry stampeded past, the exhausted Austrian infantry of the main body lost heart and rushed to the rear. The whole French infantry line advanced westward.
phases.quote: the exhausted Austrian infantry of the main body lost heart, provoking a wild rush to the rear.
